Getting around

Walk the Mall and monuments; use Metrorail for everything further out.

  • ✓Metro ★Metrorail is fast and clean; fares about $2-6 depending on distance and time.
  • ✓BusMetrobus covers the city; fares are low and exact change or a card is needed.
  • ✓Taxi / ride appsUber and Lyft work well; taxis are metered and easy to find downtown.
  • ✓Rental carDriving is stressful: heavy rush-hour traffic, confusing parking rules and toll lanes.
  • ✓Walking ★Walking is the best way to see the Mall and monuments; bikeshare docks are everywhere.
  • ✓Water taxiNo ferry service in the city centre; the Potomac water taxi links some waterfront spots.
Recommended stay★ 2 nights (3 days)

Two nights covers the Mall monuments and the main free museums; add a night for Arlington and a day trip.

Best for
  • HistoryThe Mall monuments, the Smithsonian museums and Ford's Theatre.
  • CultureFree museums, the Kennedy Center and neighbourhood markets.
  • FamilyAir and Space, the Zoo and the National Archives, mostly free.

Climate

Four clear seasons: cold winters, warm humid summers, and the best weather in spring and autumn.

  • 🌸Best time: April, May, September, OctoberHighs of roughly 19–26°C and comfortable walking weather for the Mall and monuments.
  • 🥵Summer is hot and humidJuly and August reach about 30–31°C with muggy air. Do outdoor sights in the morning.
  • 🧥Winter is genuinely coldJanuary highs near 6°C and lows around -2°C. Bring a proper coat, hat and gloves.
  • 🌧️Rain is spread through the yearAbout 8–14 rain days a month, most in summer. A small umbrella is worth packing.
  • ☀️Long summer daysJune and July give long daylight for evening monument walks; winter days are short.
  • 🧳What to packComfortable walking shoes, layers, a rain jacket, sunscreen in summer and a warm coat in winter.

Landmarks 30

Must-see · 8

  1. 1

    Lincoln Memorial

    The Lincoln Memorial is an iconic must-see with its massive statue and famous steps overlooking the Reflecting Pool. Visit early morning to avoid crowds and see the monument in soft light; it's free and open 24 hours.

  2. 2

    National Mall

    The National Mall is the heart of the capital, a grand park lined with monuments and museums. Walk it at sunrise or rent a bike to cover more ground; most monuments are free and accessible.

  3. 3

    Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

    Home to the Hope Diamond and dinosaur skeletons, this museum is a favorite for all ages. Admission is free; arrive at opening to beat the crowds, especially on weekends.

  4. 4

    The White House

    The White House is the president's residence and a symbol of American democracy. Public tours require advance requests through your member of Congress; view it from Lafayette Square if tickets aren't available.

  5. 5

    United States Capitol

    The Capitol is where Congress meets and offers free tours of the rotunda and chambers. Book tours online in advance; the visitor center is accessible via Union Station Metro.

  6. 6

    National Gallery of Art

    This world-class museum houses masterpieces from da Vinci to Van Gogh, including 'Luncheon of the Boating Party'. Free entry; start with the West Building for classic works and take a break in the sculpture garden.

  7. 7

    Washington Monument

    The Washington Monument offers the best panoramic views of the city from its observation deck. Free timed tickets are required; reserve online or arrive early for same-day tickets.

  8. 8

    Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

    See the Wright Flyer and Apollo 11 command module in this tribute to flight. Free admission; timed-entry passes are required, so book online before your visit.

    Baltimore · 1 h 02 by train

    ★★★★☆ · Full day · 62 km from Washington D.C.

    Best way: Frequent MARC and Amtrak trains from Union Station reach Baltimore Penn Station in about an hour, with the free circulator covering the last mile.

    Take a MARC Penn Line train or Amtrak from Union Station to Baltimore Penn Station, then walk or use the free Charm City Circulator to the Inner Harbor.

    • Train ★1 h 02 · from $2-$600
    • Bus1 h 01 · from $5-$26
    • Car1 h 01 · taxi ≈ $160

    What to see

    • Inner Harbor
    • National Aquarium
    • Fort McHenry
    • American Visionary Art Museum

    8 landmark quests to check off here

    Good to know

    • The Inner Harbor and Fell's Point are reachable via the free Charm City Circulator.
    • MARC Penn Line service is limited on weekends.
    • Book Amtrak ahead if you want a specific departure time.

    Alexandria · 18 min by road

    ★★★★☆ · Half day · 13 km from Washington D.C.

    Best way: The Metro Yellow or Blue Line drops you directly at King Street-Old Town, steps from the waterfront historic district.

    Take the Metro Yellow or Blue Line directly to King Street-Old Town station, then walk a few blocks to the waterfront historic district.

    • Bus17 h 31 · from $393-$1,111
    • Car18 min · taxi ≈ $40

    What to see

    • Old Town Alexandria
    • King Street
    • Torpedo Factory Art Center
    • George Washington Masonic National Memorial

    2 landmark quests to check off here

    Good to know

    • Old Town's King Street is walkable from the Metro station.
    • Weekends are lively but crowded along the waterfront.
    • Combine with a stroll to the Torpedo Factory art center.

    Annapolis · 47 min by road

    ★★★☆☆ · Full day · 52 km from Washington D.C.

    Best way: No direct train reaches downtown Annapolis and the bus route requires a transfer, so driving is clearly better for this short 47-minute road trip.

    Take a MARC Penn Line train or bus to New Carrollton, then a local bus to Annapolis, or drive; no direct train reaches downtown Annapolis.

    • Bus1 h 10 · from $5-$8
    • Car ★47 min · taxi ≈ $130

    What to see

    • U.S. Naval Academy
    • Maryland State House
    • Annapolis City Dock
    • Historic district walking tour

    Good to know

    • The historic district and Naval Academy are best explored on foot once you park.
    • Weekends in spring and fall are busiest; arrive early for parking.
    • Many downtown sights cluster near the City Dock and Main Street.

    Fredericksburg · 1 h 35 by train

    ★★★☆☆ · Full day · 84 km from Washington D.C.

    Best way: The VRE/Amtrak train runs directly to Fredericksburg station with the historic district a short walk or local bus away.

    Take a VRE Fredericksburg Line train or Amtrak from Union Station directly to Fredericksburg station, then walk or take a short local bus to the historic district.

    • Train ★1 h 35 · from $28-$45
    • Bus1 h 35 · from $10-$15
    • Car1 h 12 · taxi ≈ $210

    What to see

    • Fredericksburg Historic District
    • Hugh Mercer Apothecary Shop
    • Mary Washington House
    • Battle of Fredericksburg sites

    1 landmark quest to check off here

    Good to know

    • VRE primarily runs on weekdays, so check the schedule for weekend trips.
    • The historic district is walkable from the station.
    • Allow time to explore the battlefield sites outside downtown.

    Build my plan

    Swap in instead

    • Swap a museum morning for Arlington National Cemetery and the Changing of the Guard, across the river by Metro.
    • Take a day trip to Old Town Alexandria: shops, the waterfront and historic streets, about 30–40 minutes by Metro or train.
    • Add a Potomac water taxi ride between Georgetown and the Wharf for a different view of the city.

    Getting around

    • Metrorail is fast and clean; fares about $2-6 depending on distance and time.
    • Metrobus covers the city; fares are low and exact change or a card is needed.
    • Uber and Lyft work well; taxis are metered and easy to find downtown.
    • Driving is stressful: heavy rush-hour traffic, confusing parking rules and toll lanes.
    • Walking is the best way to see the Mall and monuments; bikeshare docks are everywhere.
    • No ferry service in the city centre; the Potomac water taxi links some waterfront spots.

    Where to stay

    • Downtown / Penn Quarter · ≈ USD 180–420 a night
      Walk to the Mall, the White House and the big museums. Most central base for a first visit.
    • Capitol Hill · ≈ USD 150–350 a night
      Quiet streets, the Capitol and Library of Congress on your doorstep; good Metro links.
    • Georgetown · ≈ USD 200–500 a night
      Pretty historic streets, shops and waterfront dining. No Metro station, so plan on buses or walking.
    • Dupont Circle · ≈ USD 160–380 a night
      Lively, central and good value; embassy mansions, cafés and a Metro stop.

    Food & drink

    • Try a half-smoke sausage, the local speciality; chili-topped is the classic order.
    • Eastern Market on Capitol Hill is good for a cheap lunch and a weekend market browse.
    • Ethiopian food along 9th Street NW and in Adams Morgan is a local favourite; sharing platters feed two.
    • The Wharf and Georgetown waterfront have sit-down seafood; book ahead on weekends.
    • Food trucks near the Mall and office districts give filling lunches for around $10–15.

    Tips

    1. All Smithsonian museums, the National Gallery of Art, and the National Zoo are completely free to enter
    2. Stand on the right and walk on the left when using the steep Metro escalators — locals will correct you if you block the left
    3. Get a SmarTrip card to ride the Metro and buses
    4. Springtime brings the famous Cherry Blossom Festival around the Tidal Basin, but it is extremely crowded
    5. The city is divided into four quadrants (NW, NE, SW, SE); pay close attention to addresses
